result.name: D12 CONTEXT
keyFindings: D12 = \industrial7\gdi-truetype-ui. It is not flipped (an open operator decision). The code change is two lines: kernel/kmain/src/win32k/font/mod.rs:621-633 and 742-747 return the 8x16 stand-in when the knob is off and the face is in UI_FAMILIES (crates/i7font-abi/src/map.rs:249). The prepared branches p9-flips 720be4c166 and p9-flips-micross 324d17594c are stale (9 merge conflicts each against dwrite-owned/m3). Their earlier verdicts ('D12 GO, micross GO after D12') need re-running.

Stand-in [i7]: every UI face at every height gives tmHeight 16, ascent 12, descent 4, intlead 0, ave 8, max 8, alphabet 416x16 (raster.rs:96-97). In the Win7 column this alone explains 852+13 comctl32 rows.

15/13 [W10 m208 CC30 and m199 NP metrics, 96 DPI]: 15 is tmHeight of Segoe UI -12 (the list view's default font = icon-title font: 15/12/3, il 3, ave 6, max 31, alphabet 347). 13 is tmHeight of MS Shell Dlg -11 = DEFAULT_GUI_FONT (13/11/2, il 2, ave 5, max 23, alphabet 323).
19/17 [W10 CC30]: SysListView32 report-view row heights. 19 with the default font, 17 after WM_SETFONT(DEFAULT_GUI_FONT); the header is 24 in both. i7 gives row 20 and header 20.

Win10 decomp: CLVView::ComputeCYItemSize (comctl32 0x86678) = max(text, image) + SM_CYBORDER, raised to text + 2*EditYPadding in views 1-2. ComputeEditYPadding (0x1a6a8) is EM_GETRECT.top of a temporary edit control in that font, so the padding depends on the font. That gives 15+4=19 and 13+4=17 (padding 2 is inferred).

Win10 decomp: Header_OnLayout (0x4b2a8) = ('...' extent cy) + 2*edge, raised to the theme min height. _Header_InitTheme sets that minimum to max(GetThemePartSize(Header, HP_HEADERITEM, TS_TRUE).cy, GetThemePosition(1,0,0xd4b).y). So the header's 24 is a theme size: D12 alone would give i7 a 19/17 header, not 24 (inference).

micross issue: with the knob on, MS Shell Dlg falls back to Arial -11 because micross.ttf is not in the base set. That gives h14 a11 d3 il3 ave5 max29, alphabet 322, versus Win7 and Win10 Microsoft Sans Serif h13 a11 d2 il2 ave5 max23, alphabet 323. The error is 1 px of descent/cell height; widths are nearly equal.
File-version trap: Win10 Segoe UI -12 max is 31, while Win7 and i7-knob-on give 23, because i7 stages the Win7 RTM segoeui.ttf v5.01. Win10 rows therefore need per-file provenance (version + sha256).

Existing data: fonts-base.i7 (29 Win7 faces + Inter, no micross, no .fon), win7-fonts.manifest.tsv (436 files with sha256; micross 32a9b170... v5.02), fontlink-fonts.sha256, gdi32 *.win7.tsv / *.ui.tsv tables (fonts_sysfont, fonts_metrics, fonts_widths, text_extent, ...), and bb depot Win10 runs m188/m199-m202/m208 (96 DPI only).

The DATA REQUIREMENTS table R1-R12 covers: font file provenance; FontSubstitutes/SystemLink; TEXTMETRIC/OTM/realization for faces x heights x weights x DPI; widths/ABC; extents for a fixed string set; stock objects; list view geometry with EditYPadding; header theme part sizes; other comctl32 controls; dialog base units and MapDialogRect; glyph bitmap hashes. Each has a line-oriented TSV format.

result.name: 04 Wine and tools eval
keyFindings: Wine is not a usable oracle. Same exe, 27 rows (9 faces x 3 heights): Wine matches Win10 on tmHeight in 14/27 rows and tmMaxCharWidth in 3/27. Segoe UI -12 gives h=14 in Wine against h=15 on Win10 (internal leading 1 against 3). Wine only agrees for the bitmap fonts (MS Sans Serif, System) and for the Tahoma-like substitutes (Tahoma and MS Shell Dlg 2: same cell heights and extents, but tmMaxCharWidth 16/17/23 against 27/29/39). Segoe UI is not installed in Wine, and Wine echoes the requested face name back from GetTextFace. Wine's EnumFontFamiliesEx count is 794 against 682 on Win10. Wine is useful only to check that a probe compiles, runs and prints.
tools/wine_run.sh uses the Proton-GE wine-11.0 Staging build by default, not the system wine-9.0. I ran only the 11.0 build.
Host tools present: xorriso 1.5.6, qemu 8.2.2, python 3.12 with PIL 10.2, numpy 1.26 and fontTools 4.46, plus x86_64 and i686 mingw. freetype-py is missing.

LAB_READY was present when tested (Win10 build 19045.2965). Hello probe through win10_run.sh took 40 s end to end. The guest auto-logs on as Administrator at 1024x768, 96 dpi, 32 bpp. boot.cmd does not relay run.cmd stdout, so output must be redirected to COM1.
Both COM1 routes work and give byte-identical output: 'exe > COM1' and CreateFileA(\\.\COM1) with WriteFile (no SetCommState needed). Probe stdout lines arrive LF, while cmd echo lines arrive CRLF.

Binary transfer works: certutil -encode then 'type > COM1' moved 200000 bytes in about 1.2 s (roughly 220 KB/s) with a matching sha256 after base64 -d. Boot and shutdown account for about 35 s of the 40 s.
Earlier bb depot probes (m192, m205) import only GDI32, KERNEL32 and USER32 and write to stdout with WriteFile; run.cmd does the redirect.

Real Win10 numbers I ran: Segoe UI -12 is 15/12/3 (height/ascent/descent) with ave 6 and max 31, matching the np_metrics probe (bb depot m199). Segoe UI -11 is 13, Tahoma -11 is 13, and MS Shell Dlg -11 is 13 with -12 also 13 (stepping to 20 at -16).

Unexplained: Win10 Arial -11 gives cell height 14 with internal leading 3, which looks too tall for Arial's metrics. The probe used a 1bpp memory DC. I recommend an A/B against GetDC(NULL) in the first real data run.
